checksumDefinition: base64(SHA-512/256) over the (decompressed) file bytes except the root-level checksum line and its terminator (FASTA, GFA, FHP FASTA and FHGFF3 only; in microdata and JSON-LD the checksum is an ordinary metadata value)

R1.summary: Checksum rule 1: hash the exact file bytes without normalization; for gzip/BGZF input, the decompressed bytes.

R2.summary: Checksum rule 2: exactly one root-level checksum line with an unquoted key; spaces only to match root indentation and before the colon; nested checksum properties stay covered.

R3.summary: Checksum rule 3: exclude that entire line and its terminator; hash every other byte, so changing covered bytes invalidates the checksum.

R4.summary: Checksum rule 4: SHA-512/256 digest in standard padded base64, no prefix.

R5.summary: Header parsing: the checksum value is a single-line YAML scalar on the checksum line; block scalars and continuation lines are invalid.

R6.summary: Header parsing: FHR header lines are UTF-8 without U+0085, U+2028 or U+2029; bytes outside header lines are not decoded.

R7.summary: Header parsing: a FASTA/GFA file must not begin with a UTF-8 byte order mark.

R8.summary: Header parsing: no duplicate mapping keys, YAML anchors, aliases or merge keys.

R9.summary: Header parsing: in microdata the first of repeated attributes applies; itemtype and itemprop are space-separated token lists.

R10.summary: Header parsing: FHR lines form the leading header block; a later FHR line, including one from a concatenated file, is invalid.

M1.summary: Microdata: exactly one FHR item scope; a nested item scope without itemprop is a separate item whose properties do not leak.

M2.summary: Microdata: HTML parsing with implied end tags; values come from the defining element's value attribute, else its text.

M3.summary: Microdata: data-fhr-type values must match the declared JSON type; typed strings are exact; untyped schema numbers and lists are converted.

M4.summary: Microdata: the extracted metadata must validate against fhr.json; a repeated property cannot fill a single-valued field.

J1.summary: JSON-LD: a canonical document has a published FHR context (embedded or a known URL) and no keyword but @type and a root @id; @context and @type are set aside, subjectOf is documentation, and export terms are set aside.

J2.summary: JSON-LD: duplicate object keys are invalid.

J3.summary: JSON-LD: any other form is read by JSON-LD 1.1 expansion with bundled contexts only; a context that is not bundled, remote or unknown, is invalid.

J4.summary: JSON-LD: exactly one top-level node (directly or the only item of @graph); every property must map to an FHR field in its scope, and unknown terms or a root @id make the document invalid.

J5.summary: JSON-LD: IRI fields take @id or a string; dateCreated takes xsd:date or no type, and no other datatype is allowed; single-valued fields take one value; commandLineOption comes from @list; a node given only by @id is invalid.

J6.summary: JSON-LD: the resulting metadata must validate against fhr.json.

J7.summary: JSON-LD: writers emit the record with an embedded context and typed nodes, byte for byte as docs/JSONLD.md describes.
J7.notApplicable: J7 constrains writers; a reader has no invalid input for it. The valid vectors that cite J7 are writer output.

P1.summary: FHP: the metadata of a protein FASTA header must validate against fhp.json.

P2.summary: FHP: a record is read as FHP only when its schema is an FHP schema URL; any other header is validated as FHR.

G1.summary: FHGFF3: line 1 is ##gff-version 3; the leading header block runs from line 2 to the first nonblank line that is not a # line, or to ##FASTA; #~ lines may be mixed with other # lines inside it, and a #~ line on line 1 or after it is invalid.

G2.summary: FHGFF3: the metadata must validate against fhgff3.json, including the genome link (an annotates link to an FHR genome, a genomeReference, or both).

G3.summary: FHGFF3: a record is read as FHGFF3 only when its schema is an FHGFF3 schema URL; any other header is validated as that type.

V1.summary: Selection: the raw-main URL of a type's schema file selects the current schema of that type; there is no fallback to an older release.

V2.summary: Selection: a release's raw tag URL (.../FHR-Specification/vX.Y.Z/<file>) selects that release's schema of the file's type.

V3.summary: Selection: a w3id URL https://w3id.org/fair-bioheaders/<type>/vX.Y.Z (trailing slash allowed) selects that release's schema of the type, including older releases.

V4.summary: Selection: a release that the reader does not have, a release without a schema of that type, or a raw URL with any other ref gives an unsupported-version result, never another schema.

V5.summary: Selection: any other schema value is FHR, validated against the current FHR schema.
